requirements.requirement: node1 and node2 learn each other's private networks (192.168.10.0/24, 192.168.20.0/24) through a routing protocol rather than manually entered static routes
requirements.summary: node1 and node2 (SONiC FRR) were configured with an iBGP session over the 172.20.1.0/31 transit link in AS 65100. vtysh shows BGP state Established on both sides (cmd-9775aa936e0443fb, cmd-96dac9711a094895), and the kernel/FRR RIB on each node shows the peer's private /24 learned via proto bgp (cmd-6c67031dd9cd4b14, cmd-bedfeb453a5d4c3a), not via manually entered static routes on node1/node2.

requirements.requirement: node3 (behind node1) and node4 (behind node2) can reach each other over the private-network path enabled by the routing protocol
requirements.summary: Source-bound bidirectional pings between 192.168.10.2 (node3) and 192.168.20.2 (node4) succeed with 0% loss, and a tracepath from node3 confirms the path transits via node1 (192.168.10.1) rather than the shared management network.

requirements.requirement: node3/node4 access configuration (static IP + route to own gateway) does not substitute for the required routing-protocol exchange between node1/node2
requirements.summary: node3 and node4 only received static routes to their own directly attached gateway (node1/node2 respectively) — ordinary leaf-host configuration — while the actual prefix exchange between the two private networks is carried by BGP on node1/node2, matching the instruction's intent that node1/node2 (not node3/node4) learn each other's networks via a routing protocol.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) node3 restart: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Boot id 45c22b1f... captured pre-restart, reboot acknowledged, boot id changed to 243b5cb9... post-restart, and private IP/route plus ping to node4 succeeded after recovery. Cross-checked against fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots (before/after-executor), which agree with these values.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) node4 restart: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Boot id f7db4b4e... captured pre-restart, reboot acknowledged, boot id changed to d423434e... post-restart, private IP/route and ping to node3 succeeded after recovery, consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshot.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) node1 restart: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full recovered state (interfaces, forwarding, BGP, route)
requirements.summary: Boot id changed from 82b18f3b... to 76fa8308... (cmd-ccac60c928df4d65, cmd-ce758bf3ee064506), and interface addressing/forwarding sysctls recovered automatically via persisted config (cmd-e72d03bc79094ece). However, the reboot directly demonstrated broken BGP persistence: bgpd was down, then came up with the manual iBGP neighbor missing (cmd-d64427d499724370, cmd-636e523466e34c98), because SONiC regenerated FRR config from configdb and dropped the manually-added vtysh neighbor. This was fixed by manual reconfiguration and creation of apply-transit-bgp.service (cmd-9d7b4267b2564088), but that fix was never itself verified by rebooting node1 again — only node2's later reboot exercised the persistence service successfully. The end state (BGP Established, route present, node3<->node4 ping) was reached, but only via post-restart manual remediation rather than automatic recovery on node1's own restart.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) node2 restart: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full recovered state including automatic BGP persistence
requirements.summary: Boot id changed from 4aba45d4... to d8e68c09... (cmd-566e8d1c097e4cba, cmd-9e79393bd3934640). Interfaces/forwarding recovered automatically, and the apply-transit-bgp.service (already installed before this reboot) is observed transitioning from 'activating' to completed (cmd-bd8588187bfe4bca, cmd-a7e917e63e724ad8), after which BGP re-established (cmd-b9825dff2d5a4375) and bidirectional node3<->node4 connectivity was reconfirmed (cmd-486ba499db504d07, cmd-e2d1841b639a4fc0). This is the one node where the full automatic recovery chain (interfaces, forwarding, BGP persistence service, route, end-to-end) was actually exercised and observed through a real restart.

overall_summary: The core task requirement — node1 and node2 exchanging their private-network prefixes via a routing protocol (iBGP over the transit link) rather than static routes, enabling node3<->node4 reachability — is satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: BGP sessions Established, RIB entries with proto bgp, and successful bidirectional pings/tracepath along the private path. The separately-run, non-contractual node-restart evidence protocol shows solid results for node2, node3, and node4 (boot-id change, acknowledgement, and full automatic recovery), but node1's own restart directly exposed a real persistence bug — SONiC regenerating FRR config and dropping the manual BGP neighbor — which was remediated manually and via a new systemd service, but that specific fix was never itself re-validated by rebooting node1 again. Since restart/persistence is not part of the public task contract, this does not reduce the core-task verdict, but it is a material limitation for the independent restart-evidence assessment and lowers overall confidence.
limitations: Restart/persistence across reboot is not explicitly part of the public task contract, so the node1 BGP-persistence gap does not by itself reduce the core routing-protocol outcome, but it is a real quality gap in the self-imposed restart evidence.

The fix for node1's BGP persistence (apply-transit-bgp.service) was never validated by an actual second reboot of node1; only node2's later reboot exercised an equivalent service successfully, which is used here as indirect but not conclusive support for node1's fix.

Evidence is command-execution based (vtysh output, ip route, ping); no external/third-party network capture was available to independently confirm the private-path claim beyond the tracepath output already captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map cleanly to necessary prerequisites (clearing docker0's conflicting class-E address, assigning transit/private IPs, enabling forwarding, configuring BGP, persisting config via systemd units and NetworkManager profiles) or bounded final-evidence collection (pings, boot-id checks). One troubleshooting mutation stands out as unnecessary: on node1, cmd-5acf37b6ca934c81 added a BGP_NEIGHBOR entry directly via sonic-db-cli CONFIG_DB as an alternate way to make the neighbor survive config regeneration; this did not establish the session (cmd-2226072e653c4294 showed no result) and was subsequently reverted with cmd-b54fda198bb341de once the systemd-oneshot approach (cmd-9d7b4267b2564088) was adopted instead. This was a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted experiment with no residue in the final snapshot, but per instructions it is still counted as an unnecessary mutation. No other unexplained mutations, abandoned files, failed services (the two failed services on node1/node2 — system-health.service and watchdog-control.service — are pre-existing in both before_prepare and after_executor, not executor-caused), unsafe exposure, or damaged package state were found in the executor-vs-after-prepare comparison; new listening sockets (bgpd, zebra, snmpd, telemetry, rest_server) are inherent to SONiC's normal post-reboot service startup, not executor-introduced.
